blocking_todos.action:
Re-derive the identity prompt from the 640x480 corpus, or sample-check the committed
one against a random sample of episodes spanning the corpus and record the sample, the sample size
and the disagreements. If the appearance is not constant across the 402, that is the finding and
arm C needs a per-episode identity prompt rather than one shared string.
blocking_todos.claim:
[identity_style].prompt is assembled from a T-041 machine caption of ONE clip,
episode_000135_clip000 (see [source].caption_provenance), and is applied unchanged to all 402
episodes. Nobody has checked that it describes the other 401, and it was written against T-041's
corpus rather than against the 640x480 re-derivation PR-08 §3 restyles.
blocking_todos.closes_by: editing this file (status = CLOSED, plus the evidence) before the first identity clip
blocking_todos.evidence_frame_rule: one frame per episode at index round(0.1 * (n_frames - 1)), decoded forward (select=eq(n,IDX)), never seeked. Early rather than middle or late because the apple, the cloth, the background, the lighting and the plate are all unoccluded only before the transfer.
blocking_todos.evidence_required: the sampled episode ids, the sample size, and the per-episode verdicts
blocking_todos.evidence_sample_scheme: stratified-systematic/1 — episode ids sorted, split into sample_size contiguous strata of near-equal size (bounds k*M//N), one episode drawn uniformly at random inside each under sample_seed. Spans the recording order by construction; a fixed stride was rejected because it aliases with any periodicity in that order.
blocking_todos.resolution:
CLOSED 2026-08-22. The suspicion was right and the diagnosis was wrong: the
caption is not a bad generalisation from episode_000135, it is wrong about episode_000135. A census
of ALL 402 episodes measured per-episode mean cloth RGB spanning (66.1, 65.9, 65.0) to
(86.4, 86.5, 85.8) -- L* 28.0-36.7, largest in-episode R/G/B spread 3.07 counts, i.e. neutral grey.
Black cloth sits near L* 5. Not one of the 402 is close, and episode_000135 itself is
(88.2, 87.9, 89.0).

The `action` field's either/or was answered both ways. Sample-check: judged blind by a calibrated
instrument, the committed wording drew match 0 / mismatch 40, every row naming the cloth. Re-derive:
the census then fixed the two words, and the corrected wording drew match 40 / mismatch 0 on the
SAME forty frames with DISJOINT judges in the same session, so this is not judges getting friendlier.

`action` also asked what to do if the appearance is not constant across the 402 -- arm C would need a
per-episode prompt rather than one shared string. It is constant on every axis the prompt names:
cloth in a narrow neutral band, warm apple mask present 402/402 with zero green pixels in any
episode, bright plate region present 402/402, frame median luminance 79.6-95.0 corpus-wide. ONE
SHARED STRING IS THEREFORE CORRECT, and no per-episode prompt is needed.

The one genuinely inconstant feature was measured and deliberately EXCLUDED: a pale strip of the
surface behind the cloth is a full-width band in 370/402 episodes and ABSENT IN 32 (contiguous
recording runs where the camera sat lower), 3.7% of frame height at the median. Naming it would tell
an image-conditioned generator to synthesise a surface that is not there in 8% of the corpus -- the
same class of error being corrected here, in the other direction.

KNOWN AND NOT CLOSED BY THIS. (1) `and a visible stem` is a fourth false specific: the apple is
rotated so no stalk faces the camera in roughly a quarter of frames. The calibrated protocol did NOT
reproduce it as a mismatch -- all 40 rows matched, one judge noting "stem turned away from the
camera" and matching anyway -- so it was left alone rather than edited on an uncalibrated pass.
(2) Passing the instrument's calibration is necessary and never sufficient: its items are
manufactured and these forty are natural frames. (3) Every observer in the chain is a model, which
is a correlated observer to the instrument it judges. Full argument and the raw numbers:
docs/t040-identity-prompt-correction.md.
blocking_todos.rule_ref: PR-08 §5 — arm C's style prompt *is* the source's own appearance
blocking_todos.why_blocking:
Arm C is a control, and a control is only a control if its prompt is the
source's own appearance. If the caption is wrong for most episodes — a different cloth, a
different apple, different lighting — then arm C is a weak RESTYLE, not an identity pass. It would
then carry some of arm B's diversity, B - C would understate the diversity effect, and the
headline's attribution between 'diversity helped' and 'generator fingerprint' silently breaks. The
frame-match fixed by [volume] does not help here: a frame-matched control with the wrong prompt is
still the wrong control.

Contrast between the dark grey background and the white plate and red/yellow apple. Live-action video, realistic. The white plate keeps its own appearance.
